method: For each n in {64, 128, 256, 512, 1024}, build adjacency submatrix C_n on rows/cols {3,...,n} where C_n[i,j] = 1 iff j = f(i) (shortcut Collatz) and 3 <= i,j <= n. Compute trace(C_n^p) for p = 1..p_max via direct integer iteration. Theorem 3 (Paparella 2024): aperiodic Collatz on truncation iff C_n nilpotent iff tr(C_n^p) = 0 for all p.
headline_finding: Paparella's nilpotency criterion holds at every tested truncation up to n = 1024. No counterexample to aperiodic Collatz on the truncated graph. Sparsity pattern: nnz scales linearly with n at slope ~0.83 (most rows have an in-bound edge). Matrix is essentially a function-graph (each row has 0 or 1 nonzero), so nilpotency reduces to acyclicity of the truncated functional graph -- which the data confirms exactly.
interpretation: This is consistent with (and would have detected counterexamples to) Collatz aperiodicity on small truncations. As an independent linear-algebra check it complements Mori's operator-theoretic and Tao's probabilistic verifications already in the project.
